html:
Kievan Rus' was the first East Slavic state, centred on Kyiv, which lasted from the late 800s until the Mongols sacked Kyiv in 1240. Ukraine, Belarus and Russia all trace their history back to it.

Its rulers, the Rurik dynasty, came from Scandinavian traders and warriors known as Varangians, part of the wider world of Viking Age Scandinavia. According to the Primary Chronicle, Prince Oleg of Novgorod took Kyiv in 882 and made it his seat. The state grew along the river route "from the Varangians to the Greeks", which linked the Baltic to the Black Sea and Constantinople. Furs, wax, honey and slaves went south; silver and silk came north.

High points:

  • In 988 Prince Vladimir took Christianity from the Byzantine Empire, the baptism of Rus'. Orthodox Christianity, Cyrillic writing and Byzantine art followed.
  • Yaroslav the Wise (died 1054) issued a law code and built Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral; the Kyiv Monastery of the Caves was founded in his time. His daughters married into the royal houses of France, Norway and Hungary.

After Yaroslav, the land was shared among his many descendants, and Rus' became a loose family federation of principalities, often at war with each other and with steppe peoples. Novgorod in the north grew rich and nearly independent.

The Mongol invasion of 1237 to 1240 destroyed most of the cities. The lands then fell under the Golden Horde in the east and Lithuania and Poland in the west, while Moscow, a minor town, slowly rose to become Muscovy.
sum: Kievan Rus' was the first East Slavic state, centred on Kyiv, which lasted from the late 800s until the Mongols sacked Kyiv in 1240. Ukraine, Belarus and Russia all trace their history back to it.
